question: Do actual CENTER VNS exits with new archive value get rejected by PDDR often enough to justify a separate indicator-acceptance continuation probe?
scope: Existing4original-kernel100k trajectories,2developmentinstances,oldseed12390003. Allcompleted CENTER programs included; partial and other roles retained as separate counts. No replay, new candidate, altered acceptance, reference source, operator or teacher.
engineering: Independently reconstruct every actual CENTER PDDR decision from paid reference objectives and both endpoints; duplicates retained. Verify reference availableAtPaidFE and each reference point physical paid birth<=program start. Any disagreement stops engineering. counterfactual: Compare single endpoint contributions against SAME frozen100-point reference at1.25,1.5,2.0 and original normalization. Strictly prefer candidate when its reference-set HV exceeds incumbent by>1e-10. This is only a decision on old candidate pairs, not the resulting policy trajectory or measured advantage.
archiveValue: Reuse previously independently rebuilt pre-program archive endpointSingleHVgain. Only gains>1e-10 count. A newly accepted endpoint is informative only if it was actually rejected, adds value against pre-program paid archive, and counterfactual HV would accept it. Sum of conditional endpoint gains is not a unionHV or a causal gain.
gate: BOTH FULL instances: at least100completeCENTER programs; at least20 actual-rejected new-valued endpoints accepted by HV atALL3references; their summed conditional gains >=10% of all positive CENTER endpoint gains and>=1% of all completed original program sequentialHVgain. stop: If capacity fails, do not switch CENTER acceptance, add a learner, choose another reference point, select a role/window subset or run variants to rescue. Missing data not converted to negative scientific evidence. Prior identity-shake5% hypothesis remains stopped.
